claims.text: Formation and crystal-structure selection in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles are governed by competition between kinetic trapping and diffusion-driven phase separation during cooling.
Rapid quenching kinetically traps a metastable single-phase solid solution.
A controlled dwell or slower cooling provides enough time for atomic diffusion to trigger elemental segregation.
A controlled dwell or slower cooling promotes nucleation of secondary phases.
Segregated regions and secondary-phase nuclei act as transient structural mediators that redirect the final crystal structure.
The initial nanoparticles are metastable single-phase solid solutions produced under rapid heating and quenching.
The controlled intervention is to reduce the cooling rate or introduce an intermediate-temperature dwell after rapid heating.
Elemental mixing enthalpies and atomic-size mismatches influence diffusional behavior in the applicable compositional space.
Transient segregation clusters or diffusion-limited nucleation sites emerge during cooling.
Kinetic barriers under rapid quenching inhibit extensive atomic diffusion and thereby stabilize the single-phase solid solution.
Increased atomic mobility during slower cooling or a dwell facilitates elemental diffusion and segregation.
Diffusion and segregation lead to phase separation and secondary-phase nucleation.
The interplay between kinetic trapping and thermodynamic equilibration determines the final crystal structure.
Slow-cooled or intermediate-temperature-held nanoparticles will show secondary phases or elemental-distribution heterogeneity relative to rapidly quenched nanoparticles.
The hypothesis applies to alloys containing more than five noble metals.
The applicable processing window separates cooling rates fast enough to trap a single phase from rates slow enough to permit diffusion and phase separation.
The cooling-rate and dwell-time thresholds required for significant diffusion are not specified and are uncertain.
Specific elemental combinations may modulate the transformation kinetics.
The hypothesis is falsified if controlled cooling or dwelling produces no significant secondary-phase or elemental-segregation difference relative to rapid quenching.

contradictions.description: The conditions describe noble metal–based alloys comprising more than five elements, whereas the boundary narrows this to alloys containing more than five noble metals. These scopes are not equivalent because a noble metal–based alloy may include non-noble constituent elements.
